drafts.title: Mach-E Select $419 / $4,499 due - amortize before you brag
drafts.window: ~11 AM or ~2 PM MT Sunday (Sun heatmap: 5 AM; 8-9 AM; 11 AM; ~2 PM). Also 8-9 AM OK. Soft-pedal weekday 11-2 as primary for Sunday.
drafts.angle: CarsDirect updated Sep 20: 2026 Mach-E Select RWD about $419/mo for 48 months with $4,499 due (effective ~$513 before tax). Electrek factory table: ~$395/mo / avg ~$478 with $4,379 due and 15,000 miles. Kitchen-table: crossover EV payment math without rehashing Uncharted/bZ/EV6/Niro. Soft-pedal Thu Mach-E leftover identical framing; these are fresher Sep numbers.
bullets: CarsDirect (updated Sep 20, 2026): 2026 Mustang Mach-E Select RWD ~$419/mo, 48 mo, $4,499 due; effective ~$513/mo before taxes and fees; expires ~Sep 30, 2026; MSRP Select line starts ~$39,840.
Electrek manufacturer table (~Sep 5/13): Mach-E Select RWD ~$395/mo, 48 mo, $4,379 due, 15,000 mi/yr; avg monthly cost ~$478; MSRP ~$39,840; expires ~Sep 30, 2026.
Same Electrek note: Mach-E lease terms improved vs prior month; Premium RWD avg ~$499 with ~$4,674 due.
CarsDirect also shows up to ~$5,000 retail cash path and 1.9% APR combo paths (verify ZIP).
Soft-pedal Sat Uncharted / Fri EV6 / Fri Niro twins if those drafts are still unposted.
drafts.body:
A Mach-E lease ad that only shows the monthly is half a conversation.

CarsDirect still shows a 2026 Select RWD around $419 a month for 48 months with about $4,499 due. Average that drive-off and you are nearer $510 a month before tax. Electrek's factory line is a little lower on paper (~$395 / ~$478 effective) with more miles baked in. Either way, the sticky-note number is the effective monthly, not the brochure.

US kitchen-table take for a 40-year-old shopping a family crossover, or a 58-year-old who wants a simple payment stack:

1) Ask for the out-the-door sheet on the exact Select VIN, not a website monthly.
2) Divide due-at-signing by months, then add the payment. That is your real lease number.
3) Quote insurance on that VIN before you sign.
4) Map weekday Level 2 at home, work, or a real apartment plan if you rent.
5) Confirm miles/year. A 15,000-mile line can save you from overage fees if you actually drive.

35-54 line: Premium timelines save "amortize the due" math. This is a save-and-repost payment post.

55+ line: a mid-$400s lease only helps if insurance and the plug plan keep your independence.

drafts.window: ~11 AM or ~2 PM MT Sunday (Sun heatmap: 5 AM; 8-9 AM; 11 AM; ~2 PM). Also 8-9 AM OK. Soft-pedal weekday 11-2 as primary for Sunday.
drafts.angle: Cool Down / San Antonio Report (~Sep 8, 2026): CPS Energy expanding shared solar with Big Sun Solar. Customers buy 620 W panels at shared sites (~$1,240 each), get bill credits (~$115/year estimated), ~$2,300 savings over 20 years per panel. First installs on San Antonio Food Bank roof. Kitchen-table: renters and shaded roofs, NOT NY +202 MW twin, NOT NJ >=15% twin.
bullets: The Cool Down / now.solar (Sep 8, 2026): CPS Energy expanding community/shared solar; partner Big Sun Solar; open to CPS Energy account holders; aimed at renters, tree-covered homes, roofs that miss the sun.
Same piece: each panel priced ~$1,240; ~620 W panels; estimated savings ~$115/year; ~$2,300 over a 20-year program life per panel; owners can move or resell panels.
First installations use roof space leased from the San Antonio Food Bank; more Bexar County sites planned.
Soft-pedal Sat NY community solar +202 MW twin and standing NJ >=15% twin.
Soft-pedal NYC It's Electric LIVE twin (different product: curbside L2 vs shared solar).
drafts.body:
Renters keep hearing "go solar" with no roof to put it on. San Antonio just put a dollar figure on a workaround.

CPS Energy is expanding shared solar so customers can buy panels at shared sites and take the bill credits home. The early math on the Cool Down write-up: about $1,240 per 620-watt panel, roughly $115 a year in estimated savings, and around $2,300 over twenty years if the estimate holds.

US kitchen-table take (even if you are not in San Antonio):

1) Ask your utility or co-op if a shared / community solar program exists in YOUR ZIP.
2) Demand the annual savings estimate in writing, not a brochure smile.
3) Check transfer rules if you move within the same utility.
4) Compare that yearly credit to a simple rooftop quote if you own. Do not buy vibes.
5) If you rent, this is the conversation to have before you assume solar is "owners only."

35-54 line: Premium timelines share "renter solar with a price tag" stories.

55+ line: independence without a roof you own. That is the product.

drafts.window: ~11 AM or ~2 PM MT Sunday (Sun heatmap: 5 AM; 8-9 AM; 11 AM; ~2 PM). Also 8-9 AM OK. Soft-pedal weekday 11-2 as primary for Sunday.
drafts.angle: Manheim / Cox Aug 2026 index (published Sep 8) + WardsAuto Sep 11: EV wholesale index +4.5% YoY, -4.7% MoM from July; Non-EV -0.9% YoY. Cox estimates ~301,000 EV lease returns in 2026 (almost triple 2025) and ~588,688 in 2027. Kitchen-table: more choice, not a collapse panic. Soft-pedal Fri used days-to-sell twin and Tue +5.1% Recurrent twin; this is Manheim Aug softening + Cox volume numbers.

EV Index Aug: +4.5% YoY, -4.7% from July. Non-EV Index: -0.9% YoY, -0.6% MoM.

WardsAuto (Sep 11, 2026): Cox estimates ~301,000 EV lease maturities in 2026 (almost triple 2025); ~588,688 EV off-lease units in 2027 (almost double 2026); total lease maturities ~2.4M in 2026 / ~3.1M in 2027.
Same WardsAuto: seasonally adjusted average wholesale price ~$19,042 (+$68 YoY); EV index was 201.8 in August vs a June peak of 216.1 (+12% YoY then).
Soft-pedal Fri "days-to-sell" framework and Tue Recurrent +5.1% twin; keep Manheim Aug MoM soft + Cox volume as the hook.
drafts.body:
The used EV story is not "everything is crashing." It is "more cars, more choice, and a soft month after a hot first half."

Manheim's August EV index was still up about 4.5% versus a year ago, even after a 4.7% drop from July. Cox figures about 301,000 EVs coming off lease in 2026, almost triple last year, with nearly 589,000 lined up for 2027.

US kitchen-table take for a 45-year-old shopping used, or a 62-year-old who wants a reliable second car without new-car sticker shock:

1) If you are shopping used, treat August-style softness as a negotiating window, not a panic sale.
2) Pull battery health / real-world range data before you fall in love with a price.
3) Quote insurance on the VIN. Used EV insurance is still the silent deal-killer.
4) Map home or workplace Level 2 before you buy. A cheap used EV with no plug plan is expensive.
5) Compare two same-year models side by side. Volume is rising. You can walk.

35-54 line: Premium timelines save "301,000 off-lease" shopping math.

55+ line: independence is a reliable used EV with boring insurance and a plug, not a wholesale headline.
